data.title: Is TTWO a good stock to buy as GTA 6 launches?
data.description:
Take-Two Interactive shares jumped more than 6% ahead of the Grand Theft Auto VI release, but is Rockstar's blockbuster already priced into the stock?

Grand Theft Auto VI has finally arrived, ending a 13-year wait for one of the most anticipated video games in history. The launch is also generating renewed interest in Take-Two Interactive (NASDAQ: TTWO), the publicly traded parent company of Rockstar Games.

Take-Two shares surged 6.2% on Wednesday, November 18, closing at $216.61, as overwhelmingly positive early reviews fuelled expectations of record-breaking sales.

With GTA 6 launching globally on November 19 and analysts raising their revenue forecasts, investors are asking whether TTWO stock has further upside or whether the biggest gains have already happened.

Is TTWO a good stock to buy now?

Take-Two Interactive could remain an attractive investment following the GTA 6 release, particularly for investors expecting the game to generate substantial revenue beyond its initial launch.

The strongest argument for buying TTWO is that GTA 6's financial contribution is only beginning.

Take-Two's earnings potential extends beyond initial game purchases, with future opportunities from online gameplay, recurring player spending and additional platform releases.

The scale of expectations is enormous.

According to Reuters, Wells Fargo recently raised its forecast for GTA 6 sales to approximately 65 million copies during Take-Two's fiscal year ending March 2027, up from its previous estimate of 35 million.

The bank also increased its annual net bookings forecast for Take-Two by 19% to $9.76 billion.

That is considerably higher than Take-Two's own guidance of $8 billion to $8.2 billion.

However, such ambitious expectations create a risk. Even an exceptionally successful GTA 6 launch could disappoint investors if sales fail to meet Wall Street's increasingly bullish forecasts.

For investors considering TTWO shares now, the question is not simply whether GTA 6 will be successful. It is whether its success will exceed what the stock market has already priced in.

What stock is for GTA 6? Does Rockstar Games have a stock?

The stock associated with GTA 6 is Take-Two Interactive Software (NASDAQ: TTWO).

Rockstar Games, the developer behind Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption, is owned by Take-Two Interactive.

Rockstar itself is not independently listed on the stock market, meaning investors cannot purchase a separate Rockstar Games stock.

Instead, buying TTWO shares provides exposure to Rockstar's financial performance alongside Take-Two's other gaming businesses, including 2K and Zynga.

Investors searching for "GTA 6 stock", "Rockstar stock" or "Rockstar Games shares" are therefore generally looking for TTWO.

However, purchasing Take-Two shares does not mean investing exclusively in Grand Theft Auto. The company's share price also reflects its broader gaming portfolio, operating costs and financial performance.

Why has TTWO stock been falling despite the GTA 6 hype?

Take-Two has experienced considerable volatility leading up to the GTA 6 release.

Shares fell approximately 6.3% on November 16 and another 4.5% on November 17 as investors reduced exposure ahead of the launch.

Concerns about the game's enormous expectations, development costs and the possibility of investors selling after the announcement contributed to the nervousness surrounding the stock.

Take-Two also reported that fiscal second-quarter net bookings declined 18% year-on-year to $1.60 billion.

However, the stock rebounded sharply on November 18 after early GTA 6 reviews impressed investors.

Reuters reported that the game achieved a Metacritic score of 99, helping ease concerns about whether Rockstar could deliver a product capable of meeting the extraordinary hype.

The rally demonstrates how quickly sentiment can change.

It also means the earlier decline should not be confused with the latest market reaction: TTWO was rising strongly in the final regular trading session before the global launch.

Will TTWO stock go up after GTA 6 comes out?

A successful GTA 6 launch could support Take-Two's share price, but history suggests that a blockbuster release does not automatically translate into immediate stock-market gains.

Research published by IG on November 18 examined Take-Two's performance following five previous major Grand Theft Auto releases.

The stock rose over the following three months after three releases but declined after the other two.

Following GTA V's launch in 2013, Take-Two shares gained just 0.7% over three months, despite the game's enormous commercial success.

This illustrates the difference between a successful product and a successful investment.

Investors often anticipate major releases months or even years in advance. By the time a game launches, much of the expected financial benefit may already be reflected in the share price.

For GTA 6, the next major catalysts will include official sales figures, updated revenue guidance and evidence of sustained player engagement.

How high could TTWO stock go after GTA 6?

Wall Street analysts remain optimistic about Take-Two's longer-term prospects.

Wells Fargo maintained a $300 price target on November 18, implying approximately 38% upside from Wednesday's $216.61 closing price.

Other analysts have also maintained bullish forecasts, reflecting expectations that GTA 6 will produce a significant increase in Take-Two's earnings and cash generation.

However, these are analyst estimates rather than guaranteed future prices.

An important factor will be whether Take-Two can turn the enormous demand for GTA 6 into recurring revenue over several years.

The company has already demonstrated the potential of long-running gaming franchises through GTA Online, which continued generating revenue long after GTA V's original release.

If GTA 6 produces a similarly durable ecosystem, its financial contribution could extend well beyond the initial launch.

Conversely, disappointing sales figures, slower-than-expected online monetisation or weaker margins could pressure the stock.

Where can you buy GTA 6 or Rockstar stock?

Investors cannot buy Rockstar Games shares directly, but they can purchase Take-Two Interactive stock using brokers that offer access to Nasdaq-listed companies.

Platforms offering TTWO exposure include:

  1. eToro: Offers access to Take-Two Interactive (TTWO), with a stock page where eligible investors can explore the shares and place orders.
  2. XTB: Offers Take-Two shares in supported markets, alongside CFD products in certain jurisdictions.
  3. IG: Provides access to TTWO trading, with share-dealing and leveraged-product availability depending on the country and account type.
  4. Interactive Brokers (IBKR): Offers access to US-listed equities, including Nasdaq stocks, subject to account permissions and eligibility.

For investors interested in GTA 6's financial performance, purchasing actual TTWO shares provides ownership exposure to Take-Two Interactive. CFDs are different instruments and do not confer ownership of the underlying shares.

Buy Take-Two (TTWO) Stock on eToro

Should you invest in GTA 6 stock now or wait?

The case for buying Take-Two is stronger than it was before GTA 6's early reviews confirmed an enthusiastic reception.

The game has the potential to generate billions of dollars in revenue, while the wider Grand Theft Auto ecosystem could support Take-Two's earnings for years.

However, buying immediately after a sharp rally carries risks.

Investors purchasing TTWO following Wednesday's 6.2% gain are paying more than they would have before the initial review-driven surge.

Those considering a shorter-term trade may want to monitor the first official sales figures and the stock's reaction when US trading resumes on November 19.

Longer-term investors may place greater importance on Take-Two's ability to convert GTA 6's popularity into sustained earnings growth.

The decision to sell should similarly depend on whether the company's actual performance continues supporting the original investment thesis, rather than simply whether the game has launched.

The verdict: Is TTWO still a good buy?

Take-Two Interactive remains an interesting investment opportunity following the GTA 6 launch, but the stock is no guaranteed winner.

The bullish case centres on potentially record-breaking game sales, stronger future earnings and recurring revenue opportunities.

The bearish case is that expectations have already become so ambitious that even an extremely successful launch may struggle to justify further share-price gains.

With Wells Fargo forecasting as many as 65 million GTA 6 sales by March 2027, investors will be watching whether Take-Two can translate the hype into financial results.

For now, TTWO offers direct stock-market exposure to Rockstar Games and GTA 6, but investors should distinguish the game's commercial success from the price they are paying for the shares.

data.title: Nvidia stock under pressure as Colette Kress makes her first big move
data.description:
Nvidia stock (NASDAQ: NVDA) remained under pressure after interim chief executive Colette Kress moved to accelerate employee pay reviews and equity awards, seeking to steady the chipmaker following Jensen Huang’s resignation.

The stock fell 2.89% to $150.96 on Wednesday, reversing an initial post-earnings bounce despite Nvidia reporting record quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion.

At the company’s first staff meeting since Huang stepped down, Kress outlined plans to bring forward annual compensation reviews from March to December.

The decision comes as employees question Nvidia’s future leadership and investors assess whether its extraordinary AI growth can continue without its founder.

Kress brings forward pay reviews amid leadership uncertainty

Kress addressed staff at Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters on Wednesday alongside board chair Harvey Jones and senior executives, according to CNBC.

She urged employees to move forward and promised earlier reviews of salaries and stock-based awards, an important part of compensation at the chipmaker.

The schedule will shift to December from March, although the announcement does not mean every employee immediately receives an identical raise.

The move comes amid calls from some employees for Huang’s reinstatement and fears about retaining talent following his departure. A sharp fall in Nvidia stock has also reduced the market value of existing equity awards.

For investors, retaining engineers and managers matters because product launches, customer relationships and the AI chip roadmap depend on teams operating without disruption.

“Huang's departure creates a leadership vacuum which nature (and investors) abhor,” Oppenheimer analyst Rich Schafer told Yahoo Finance. He withdrew his price target, citing uncertainty over Nvidia’s leadership.

Record Nvidia earnings fail to restore investor confidence

Nvidia’s fiscal third-quarter revenue jumped 103% from a year earlier to $115.8 billion. Data-centre sales rose 110% to $107.6 billion, reflecting sustained spending on processors used to train and run AI systems.

Adjusted earnings reached $2.68 a share, ahead of expectations near $2.47.

The company also projected fourth-quarter revenue of around $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, suggesting demand remains resilient despite the transition.

Nevertheless, Wednesday’s decline showed that strong financial performance has not settled questions about governance, export restrictions and the financing behind enormous data-centre projects.

According to Reuters, analysts’ average Nvidia price target slipped to $251.74 from $265.70 on Monday, even as forecasts for future profits improved.

“The quarter answers the first question the market had about Nvidia without its founder: demand did not leave with him,” Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives said.

He maintained an Outperform rating and a $225 target, but the wider market is still waiting for reassurance about execution and strategic direction.

Can Nvidia stock recover while the CEO search continues?

The board’s choice of permanent leader will shape confidence in Nvidia’s customer partnerships, AI product roadmap and regulatory response.

Pay reviews may help staff morale, but they cannot resolve governance questions alone. Investors will also watch whether Kress can maintain momentum in the Vera Rubin platform rollout and preserve relationships with major cloud customers.

Not everyone sees the sell-off as a reason to avoid Nvidia. “I'm bullish on Nvidia relative to everything else in the AI space,” veteran investor Dan Niles told Business Insider.

He said he owned Nvidia while betting against some other AI-related companies.

That selective optimism reflects a distinction between Nvidia’s current profitability and the wider sector’s financing risks.

data.title: USD/ZAR just formed a golden cross as South African rand crash continues
data.description:
The USD/ZAR pair made a strong bullish breakout, reaching its highest level since November last year. It jumped to 17.32, up sharply from the August low of 15.90. This rally may continue as the pair has just formed a golden cross pattern and moved above a crucial resistance level. 

South African rand drops as inflation rises

The USD/ZAR exchange rate continued rising after the South African statistics agency published the latest inflation report. This report showed that the headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.7% in October from the previous 0.4%. 

The surge led to an annual increase of 5.2% from the previous month’s 4.5%. The increase was lower than the expected 5.4% and was mostly because of the rising energy prices. Brent and the West Texas Intermediate (WTI) remain at an elevated level during the month.

South Africa’s inflation remained above the South African Reserve Bank’s (SARB) 3% target during the month. Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.3% month on month. This lifted the annual rate to 4.2%, from 4% previously.

The report means that the Federal Reserve may decide to hike interest rates in the final meeting of the year. The bank left interest rates unchanged at 7.25% in its September meeting. Officials hinted that they will need to hike rates again as they predicted that inflation would keep rising in the coming months. 

Another rate hike would bring interest rates to 7.50%, widening the spread with the United States. That move normally creates a good carry trade opportunity, where investors borrow money in low rate countries and invest in high interest rate ones.

The challenge, however, is that the South African economy is slowing. The price of key commodities like gold, platinum, and palladium have dropped, lowering the amount of money coming in to the country. Other metrics like the unemployment rate have worsened, while the Trump administration is removing South Africa from AGOA. 

Federal Reserve rate hike odds are rising

Meanwhile, the USD/ZAR pair has continued rising because of the ongoing US dollar surge. The DXY Index has surged to 103.87, its highest level since April last year. It has soared by over 8.7% from its lowest level this year. Indeed, the dollar has gained against other currencies, including the euro and the British pound. 

The dollar has jumped because of the rising odds that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates in the coming months. Recent macro data showed that the US created over 165k jobs last month. Also, inflation remained stubbornly high during the month. 

As a result, traders on Polymarket, Kalshi, and other prediction marketplaces are betting that the bank will hike interest rates by 0.25% in the December meeting. Indeed, some analysts expect the bank to hike rates by 0.50%.

USD/ZAR technical analysis 

USDZAR chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the USD/ZAR pair has been in a strong upward trend in the past few weeks. After days of consolidating for a few days, the pair made a strong bullish breakout this week, reaching its highest level in a year.

The pair formed an inverted head-and-shoulders pattern, a common bullish reversal pattern in technical analysis. It also formed a golden cross pattern, which happens when the 50-day and 200-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMA) cross each other. 

Therefore, the most likely scenario is where the pair drops to 16.97, its highest point in July this year. It will then bounce back, and potentially hit the pyschological level of 18.

data.title: Trump's Iran strike threat returns, but why aren't oil prices surging?
data.description:
Oil prices struggled to rally on Thursday despite reports that US President Donald Trump was considering fresh strikes against Iran, as rising inventories and recovering Middle Eastern exports kept traders focused on the prospect of excess supply.

Brent crude futures edged up 0.18% to $92.12 a barrel at 02:37 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate slipped 0.11% to $83.17.

The restrained response followed Wednesday's 1.3% fall in Brent. With a possible new military campaign under discussion, the central question is why escalating threats are no longer enough to lift crude prices decisively.

Brent crude oil price: Trump considers further strikes

Axios reported on Thursday that Trump was weighing a joint operation with Israel against Iran, although no decision had been announced.

The White House has sought assessments of possible Iranian retaliation, including attacks on oil and gas facilities in Gulf states.

Gulf leaders are urging restraint, while Israeli officials have raised concerns about suspected Iranian weapons development. Those allegations remain disputed, and Trump indicated on Wednesday that another offensive was not imminent.

Security risks are already tangible, as recent tanker incidents and attacks on regional infrastructure have complicated shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical route for global oil supplies.

Yet traders appear reluctant to price a prolonged interruption before one materialises and changes the flow of exports.

Vandana Hari, founder of Vanda Insights, described crude as caught between a “persistent geopolitical risk premium” and increasingly bearish expectations of a sizeable surplus, in comments to Reuters on Wednesday.

Oil price forecast: Recovering supply and US stockpiles restrain prices

The International Energy Agency reported that global oil production climbed by 2.3 million barrels a day in October to 105.4 million, as Gulf exports recovered despite continued attacks.

Observed worldwide inventories rose by 52 million barrels, their first monthly increase since June. The agency expects supply to exceed demand in the fourth quarter, although diesel supplies and onshore stocks remain tight.

US data reinforced the bearish case. Commercial crude inventories increased by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million in the week ended 13 November, according to figures released Wednesday by the Energy Information Administration.

Gasoline stocks rose 5.2 million barrels, while distillate inventories gained 1.6 million. Those builds suggest refiners and distributors have more immediate supply available, weakening the case for a sustained crude rally.

But the recovery remains exposed to sudden setbacks.

Recent attacks near Hormuz “highlight the fragility of this recovery”, Sparta Commodities analyst Abhishek Kumar said in comments reported by The Wall Street Journal on Wednesday.

His warning underscores that an improving global crude balance does not mean tankers, refineries or fuel markets are secure.

Could another escalation push Brent back towards $100?

An actual interruption to Gulf shipments could change the calculation quickly, particularly if retaliation damages export terminals or closes shipping routes.

Goldman Sachs recently raised its December Brent forecast to $105 from $90, reflecting the risk of renewed supply losses. That estimate is a forecast rather than a guaranteed response to Trump's deliberations.

However, without significant disruption, recovering OPEC+ output and stronger Russian crude exports could continue limiting gains.

ING strategists Ewa Manthey and Warren Patterson wrote on Wednesday that they expect the oil balance to loosen as supply recovers, “limiting the scope for a sustained rebound in prices”.

Higher US interest-rate expectations and a firm dollar may also restrain consumption and make oil more expensive for overseas buyers.

The next decisive signals will come from Washington's military choices, tanker traffic through Hormuz and subsequent inventory figures.

data.title: Anthropic IPO prices at $83 a share as ANT prepares Thursday debut
data.description:
Anthropic has priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, according to CNBC and Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter, $5 above the top of the $70–$78 range in the company's latest SEC filing.

Class A shares in the Claude developer are due to begin trading on Thursday, 19 November, on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT.

The $83 price has not yet been locked in a prospectus supplement.

As of late evening in London on 18 November, no Form 424B4 had appeared on EDGAR, and Anthropic had not published a pricing announcement on its newsroom or IPO site.

Until a filing appears, these figures should be read as reported terms, not as a confirmed prospectus price.

Bloomberg also said the size of the offering has increased, without disclosing a new share count.

The marketed deal, in Amendment No. 3 to Anthropic's Form S-1, filed on 17 November, was 825 million Class A shares — 801,351,354 sold by the company and 23,648,646 by existing holders.

On that marketed count, $83 a share would raise $68.475 billion before underwriting discounts, an Invezz calculation.

Actual gross proceeds would be higher if the deal was upsized, as Bloomberg reported. Anthropic would not receive the proceeds from the secondary shares. A separate $26 billion private placement of non-voting Class N shares is due to close at the IPO price.

How does $83 compare with the filed range?

The official range was never raised in a filing. Amendment No. 3 still estimated $70.00 to $78.00 a share. At $78, the 825 million shares would have raised $64.35 billion gross, as set out in our note on Anthropic's $70–$78 IPO price range.

Earlier on Wednesday, CNBC reported that Anthropic was considering selling more than 825 million shares and was weighing a price well above $80.

The Wall Street Journal had reported on 17 November that Anthropic expected to price above $80, and said that would value the company at about $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion.

The prospectus granted the underwriters, represented by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, a 30-day option to buy up to 123.75 million additional Class A shares. Whether that greenshoe was resized with any upsizing of the base deal has not been disclosed.

What valuation does $83 imply?

The filing does not state a single official valuation, and the final figure will depend on the share count used, including any upsizing.

Coverage of the prospectus has put the fully diluted value at about $1.405 trillion at the $78 top of the range. A like-for-like move to $83 would imply about $1.50 trillion. That is an illustration, not a number in a pricing prospectus, and it would change if more shares have been added.

How strong was demand?

CNBC reported on Wednesday morning that institutional demand was around $400 billion and that retail demand was approaching $100 billion. Those figures were described as indications of interest, not binding orders.

What happens next?

Trading is scheduled to start on Thursday under the ANT ticker. Nasdaq, in Data Technical News #2026-28, said Anthropic's Class A common stock is expected to begin trading on 19 November.

Hargreaves Lansdown has told UK applicants that trading is expected from 2:30pm London time (9:30am ET). Investors who received an allocation pay the IPO price; anyone buying once the shares are listed pays the market price. A Form 424B4, when it appears, would be the official confirmation of the price, the final share count and any change to the greenshoe.

If ANT starts trading on 19 November, MSCI has said it would decide on early inclusion no later than before the open of the third trading day, which would be Monday, 23 November. If the stock qualifies, addition would be effective as of the close on 30 November, or 1 December.

FTSE Russell has deferred fast entry because of Thanksgiving: Russell US addition, if confirmed, would be effective 14 December, and FTSE GEIS on 21 December. Nasdaq has not issued a notice adding ANT to the Nasdaq-100. The S&P 500 is not in prospect at listing.

📘 If you are looking to trade the shares on day one, our guide on how to buy Anthropic stock walks through the steps for buying US-listed shares.

📅 We are tracking the price, valuation and timetable on our Anthropic IPO date, valuation and ticker hub.

Thursday's first trade will test whether that demand holds up in public.

data.title: Nasdaq futures jump 560 points: 5 things to know before Wall Street opens
data.description:
US stock futures climbed on Thursday as Anthropic's record-breaking initial public offering revived enthusiasm for artificial intelligence shares after five consecutive declines in the S&P 500.

Nasdaq 100 futures rose 2.06%, or 560 points, while S&P 500 contracts gained 1.12% and Dow futures advanced 0.71%.

The rally followed Wednesday's uneven session, when Nvidia fell despite upbeat earnings and investors digested hawkish Federal Reserve minutes.

Anthropic's Nasdaq debut will test appetite for richly valued technology companies.

Walmart's results, fresh labour-market data and the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI provide other reasons for investors to watch Thursday's opening bell.

5 things to know before Wall Street opens

1. Anthropic's $81 billion IPO tests the AI trade

The Claude developer priced 980 million shares at $83 each, above its marketed $70–$78 range, valuing the company at roughly $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

Trading is expected to begin Thursday on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, although the first trade may come later.

The offering helped lift European semiconductor shares even as investors questioned the economics of AI infrastructure.

2. Fed minutes keep a December hike in focus

Minutes of the October meeting showed almost all officials expected further tightening if the economy developed as forecast. Some also considered whether inflation might require a larger increase.

Markets assigned roughly 92% odds to a quarter-point December hike and an 8% chance of a half-point move.

Higher borrowing costs threaten equities despite Thursday's rally. Initial jobless claims, expected at 198,000, and the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing survey are due at 8:30 am ET.

3. Walmart earnings test consumers before the holidays

The retailer is scheduled to release fiscal third-quarter results at 7 am ET, with a conference call an hour later.

Analysts tracked by S&P Global's Visible Alpha expect about $187.3 billion in revenue and earnings of $0.64 a share.

Investors will focus on grocery demand, online sales, margins and whether shoppers are trading down to cheaper goods.

Guidance may indicate whether households can withstand inflation and borrowing costs. Alibaba and PDD Holdings also reported on Thursday, providing a parallel view of Chinese consumers.

4. Asian tech stocks tumble despite stronger Nvidia results

Taiwan's Taiex fell about 4.4%, signalling that enthusiasm for Anthropic had not erased concerns about chip valuations.

Nvidia ended Wednesday down 2.9% even after reporting $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue and forecasting around $130 billion for the next quarter.

Its interim management faces questions about margins, export controls and the cost of supplying increasingly powerful AI systems. Europe showed the opposite early reaction, with ASML and other technology-linked shares gaining.

5. Take-Two faces a high-stakes GTA VI launch

Rockstar Games is releasing Grand Theft Auto VI on Thursday, giving Take-Two Interactive a rare consumer-entertainment catalyst amid the macroeconomic and AI headlines.

Take-Two shares rallied on Wednesday as early reviews strengthened sales expectations. Wells Fargo analysts raised their estimate for units sold in the publisher's fiscal year to 65 million from 35 million and lifted their bookings forecast to $9.76 billion.

That exceeds Take-Two's earlier $8 billion–$8.2 billion guidance. Sales momentum could also influence expectations for console makers and the wider gaming industry.

data.title: Who is Rene Haas? The former Nvidia insider who could replace Jensen Huang
data.description:
Rene Haas, chief executive of Arm, has emerged as a contender to lead Nvidia following Jensen Huang’s resignation, putting a former company insider in a closely watched succession contest.

Nvidia’s recruitment firm, Heidrick & Struggles, contacted Haas about the role, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday. No formal job offer or acceptance has been announced.

The approach highlights Haas’s seven years under Huang and his subsequent record of taking Arm public and expanding its presence in artificial intelligence.

Investors are weighing whether that combination makes him a credible successor to a founder who shaped Nvidia’s strategy for more than three decades.

Seven years inside Nvidia give Haas an advantage

Haas, 64, joined Nvidia in 2006 and served as vice-president and general manager of its computing products business until 2013. Arm says he oversaw one of Nvidia’s largest revenue contributors.

An electrical and electronics engineering graduate of Clarkson University, Haas also completed executive education at Stanford. Earlier roles included positions at chip companies Tensilica and Scintera Networks.

His experience matters because Nvidia’s next chief executive will inherit an unusually technical organisation, alongside relationships built around Huang’s personal influence.

“He spent seven years at Nvidia and understands Jensen’s culture,” Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at The Futurum Group, wrote on X, according to Fortune.

Boloor also noted that Nvidia’s Grace and Vera processors use Arm technology, giving Haas an understanding of an important part of its AI platforms.

However, he left Nvidia before its recent expansion into large-scale AI systems, meaning his experience cannot guarantee a smooth transition.

The attraction is his combination of institutional familiarity and years managing relationships across the semiconductor industry.

How Haas turned Arm towards AI infrastructure

Haas joined Arm in October 2013, first overseeing strategic alliances before becoming chief commercial officer and later leading its intellectual-property products business.

He became chief executive in February 2022 and steered Arm through its Nasdaq listing in September 2023.

Since then, the company has pushed beyond licensing processor designs into more complete computing systems and, increasingly, finished silicon.

Arm’s fiscal second-quarter revenue climbed 27% to $1.44 billion, with licensing revenue up 50% to $773 million. Data-centre royalties doubled as cloud providers adopted more Arm-based processors.

The company has also indicated potential revenue of up to $2 billion from its new AGI CPU business across fiscal 2027 and 2028.

Haas took on an additional role as chief executive of SoftBank Group International in April, broadening his responsibilities across the Japanese investor’s technology portfolio.

“It's not a perfect fit by any means,” StoneX analyst Cody Acree told CBS News, although he said Haas had the design expertise to run Nvidia’s technical organisation.

Arm’s licensing-led business remains far smaller than Nvidia’s hardware and software operation. Running one successfully is not the same as managing the other.

Can a former insider replace Jensen Huang?

Nvidia appointed finance chief Colette Kress interim CEO after Huang resigned on 12 November. Its board has engaged Heidrick & Struggles to consider internal and external candidates, including executives beyond Haas.

The leadership search comes despite exceptional trading results. Nvidia reported quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, and forecast about $130 billion for the next quarter.

Yet its shares fell 2.89% to $150.96 on Wednesday, reflecting lingering uncertainty about governance and management continuity.

ATFX analyst Nick Twidale told Reuters the company needed “not only a new CEO, but probably a new operating style”, given Huang’s central role.

An appointment could also raise questions about Haas’s responsibilities at Arm and SoftBank, as well as the commercial ties between Arm and Nvidia.

data.title: Ethereum price risks crashing to $1,500 as ETF outflows mount
data.description:
Ethereum (ETH) faces the possibility of another significant decline as persistent institutional withdrawals, weakening technical indicators, and growing macroeconomic uncertainty continue to pressure the cryptocurrency.

The second-largest cryptocurrency recently broke below the important $1,850 support level, increasing concerns that its correction could extend toward $1,500 in the coming weeks.

The current price action suggests that the broader bearish trend remains intact, although deeply oversold conditions could trigger a temporary recovery before another decline.

The outlook comes as US spot Ethereum exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have experienced seven consecutive weeks of net withdrawals totaling approximately $2.4 billion.

Ethereum ETF outflows continue despite consolidating price action

Institutional sentiment toward Ethereum has deteriorated considerably in recent weeks. US spot Ethereum ETFs have recorded seven consecutive weeks of net outflows, with approximately $2.4 billion withdrawn during that period.

The withdrawal continued this week, with $54.5 million redeemed by institutional investors from Monday to Wednesday. 

The sustained withdrawals suggest that investors are reducing exposure to ETH amid heightened market uncertainty.

Persistent inflationary pressure, rising energy prices, and uncertainty surrounding the conflict involving Iran are major factors contributing to the weaker investment environment.

These developments have complicated expectations for US monetary policy, with investors increasingly concerned about the possibility of tighter financial conditions.

Ethereum price outlook: ETH stays below $1,800 as analysts target $1,500

Ethereum's decline below $1,800 represents an important technical development. The level previously served as a significant accumulation area during August, when buyers helped support a strong recovery.

However, the latest breakdown suggests that the region has failed to hold as support. If the bearish trend persists, Ethereum could extend its decline towards the $1,500 psychological level. 

This level corresponds with an important historical support region that helped stabilize Ethereum during previous corrections.

A decline toward $1,500 would also bring ETH closer to the lows recorded in June 2026. The selling pressure could intensify if trading volumes remain weak and buyers fail to return.

Under that scenario, Ethereum could extend its decline toward $1,400, revisiting the price region last seen during its April 2025 bearish trend.

Despite the negative technical outlook, Ethereum's momentum indicators suggest that the recent decline may be becoming overstretched.

The daily Relative Strength Index (RSI) has fallen into deeply oversold territory for the first time since June. The RSI currently reads 26, within the oversold region.  Historically, similar readings have preceded notable recoveries in Ethereum's price.

This could see Ethereum experience a relief rally in the short term, with the first potential recovery target standing near $1,900.

A sustained move above this level could allow ETH to challenge higher resistance, potentially extending toward $2,400.

However, the recovery could be temporary if broader market conditions remain unfavorable. Under its bearish scenario, Ethereum could rebound before eventually resuming its decline toward $1,500.

Could Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade support a recovery?

Ethereum's upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade represents another development that could influence its longer-term outlook.

The network's developers are preparing the upgrade for the final quarter of 2026, following earlier improvements introduced through the Pectra upgrade.

Although network upgrades can improve blockchain functionality and strengthen Ethereum's long-term competitiveness, their effect on token prices is not always immediate.

Nevertheless, continued development remains important for Ethereum's long-term position in the cryptocurrency industry.

data.title: Soybean price analysis: Brent oil price bounces off crucial support
data.description:
Soybean price is trading within a rather tight range as investors weigh the energy market and the overall supply/demand dynamics. The bulls attempts of a breakout late last week were unsuccessful as the differing factors failed to attract enough buyers. In the short term, sideways trading may continue, with a breakout being dependent on crucial resistance levels. 

Soybean price trades sideways amid a volatile energy market

CBOT soybean price has been trading sideways in recent sessions after easing from the bullish WASDE report. USDA’s forecast for the 2026/27 season included increased exports and lower ending stocks. This is despite the predicted surge in US production by 12 million bushels. US soybean exports are expected to increase by 25 million bushels while the global ending stocks have been lessened by 0.8 million tons. 

According to the latest NASS crop progress report, soybean harvesting is 96% complete across the United States. This is slightly higher than the average pace of 95%. 

At the same time, the Export Inspections data indicate that soybean shipments for the week that ended on 12th November were 1.708 million metric tonnes (MMT). This was a decline of 10.8% from the previous week, but an increase of 41.7% from a similar period in 2025. Notably, China was the leading destination with a shipment of 691,670 MT. Increased US exports and brisk Chinese demand continue to support soybean prices. 

However, a stronger US dollar and weaker Brazilian Real are curbing the asset’s price gains. Earlier on Tuesday, the  Brazilian Real extended its losses to a fresh 19-month low before easing slightly. Over the past three weeks, the South American currency has plunged by close to 15%, enticing local producers to increase export volumes for more US dollars. At the same time, a stronger greenback renders the dollar-priced asset more expensive for buyers holding foreign currencies. 

In the ensuing sessions, investors within the soybean market will also be eyeing crude oil prices. The crude oil market has been rather volatile in recent sessions amid conflicting drivers. On the one hand, the persistent conflicts in the Middle East are offering steady support to energy prices. However, investors are increasingly betting on a global supply glut. Crude oil prices largely impact the demand for biofuel. In addition to corn and sugarcane, soybean is a major source of biofuel.  

Soybean price technical analysis

CBOT soybean futures made subtle movements on Tuessday as the agricultural commodity continues to trade sideways. Late last week, the bulls attempted a breakout, surging to a one-and-a-half week high at $12.41 a bushel before easing back to its tight trading range. At the time of writing, soybean price was at $12.29, up by 0.04%.  

A look at its daily chart points to continued sideways trading in the short term, as investors eye the driving fundamentals and technical indicators. To begin with, CBOT soybean price remains below the short-term 25-day EMA and the medium-term 50-day EMA. Indeed, in late October, the two technical indicators formed a bearish death-cross pattern that is still in place. The bearish formation occurs when short-term MA crosses the medium/long-term MA to the downside as an indication of further losses. Besides, its RSI of 46 supports the thesis on curbed gains and range-bound trading. 

Even with these bearish technical indicators, soybean price continues to trade above the long-term 200-day EMA. This is an indication that the long-term support is still intact.  

In line with these technical indicators, and the fundamentals, the range between the support level of $12.14 and the resistance along the 25-day EMA at $12.35 is worth watching. Further gains will likely be curbed at $12.41. On the flip side, additional losses will invalidate this cautious thesis as the sellers eye the lower support level at $12.09.

data.title: Evening digest: Anthropic IPO demand surges as gold and oil prices fall
data.description:
US markets faced mixed signals on Wednesday as Anthropic prepared to price its highly anticipated initial public offering amid exceptional investor demand.

Oil prices fell more than 2% after US crude and fuel inventories recorded larger-than-expected increases, while gold dropped to its lowest level in more than a year as hawkish Federal Reserve commentary strengthened the dollar and Treasury yields.

Nvidia shares also extended their losing streak as US lawmakers sought answers over alleged export control violations and reports involving former CEO Jensen Huang.

Anthropic IPO attracts nearly $500B in demand

Anthropic is considering increasing the size of its IPO and pricing shares above the initial range of $70 to $78, CNBC reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The company closed its order books on Tuesday, with institutional demand reaching approximately $400 billion and retail demand approaching $100 billion.

These indications of interest are non-binding, and the final offering terms remain subject to change.

Anthropic initially planned to offer 825 million shares, potentially raising up to $64.35 billion at the top of its proposed price range.

The company is expected to announce its final IPO price after Wednesday's market close.

The listing is a significant test of investor appetite for AI companies.

Anthropic's proposed offering has attracted more demand than SpaceX's IPO, which raised $85.7 billion in June.

The company's prospectus reported revenue of $33.24 billion for the nine months ended September 30, an increase of approximately 1,200% year over year.

However, it recorded a net loss of $104 billion during the period, largely reflecting changes in the fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities.

Its run-rate revenue reached approximately $81 billion at the end of October.

Oil prices fall as US inventories surge

Oil prices declined after the US Energy Information Administration reported larger-than-expected increases in crude and fuel inventories.

Brent crude futures fell 1.7% to $91.50 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate dropped 3.7% to $82.80.

Both benchmarks were on track to lose approximately 20% in November amid expectations of a global supply surplus.

US crude inventories increased by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million barrels in the week ended November 13, significantly exceeding expectations for a 58,000-barrel rise.

Gasoline stocks climbed by 5.2 million barrels, compared with forecasts for a 1.6 million-barrel increase.

Distillate inventories also rose by 1.6 million barrels.

Rising Middle Eastern exports have added to expectations of greater supply, although the US-Iran conflict continues to threaten shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

Recent attacks on commercial vessels and infrastructure in the region have highlighted the risks to oil transportation.

Gold hits one-year low as rate hike expectations rise

Gold prices dropped 3% to $3,729.28 an ounce, reaching their lowest level since September 2025. US gold futures declined 3.4% to $3,732.10.

A stronger US dollar and rising Treasury yields weighed on the precious metal as investors increased expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank needed a more aggressive response to inflation, either through a 50-basis-point increase in December or a faster pace of rate hikes in 2027. Other officials have also indicated that additional increases may be necessary.

Markets priced in a 92% probability of a 25-basis-point December rate hike and an 8% chance of a 50-basis-point increase, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Silver fell 5.3%, platinum declined 4.6%, and palladium lost 2.6%.

Nvidia stock extends losing streak amid congressional probe

Nvidia shares fell 2.5%, extending their decline to a fifth consecutive session as the House Committee on Energy and Commerce demanded a formal briefing over alleged export control violations.

Committee chairman Brett Guthrie requested that interim CEO Colette Kress arrange for company officials to appear before lawmakers by December 2.

The inquiry involves Singapore-based Nvidia customer Megaspeed and allegations that it helped Chinese companies circumvent US export restrictions.

Lawmakers are also examining claims that Nvidia's general counsel contacted Commerce Department officials seeking information about the investigation.

Despite the scrutiny, analysts remain positive about Nvidia's business outlook.

The company reported third-quarter revenue of $115.84 billion, up 103.2% year over year, and forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion.

Wedbush raised its price target to $293 from $275, while RBC and Morgan Stanley maintained positive ratings.

Nvidia's remaining $227.3 billion share buyback authorisation could also provide support for the stock.
